setup: Unbeaten, top-ranked Miami visits Chapel Hill at 7:30 p.m. Eastern on ABC after scoring 52 points against Pittsburgh. Darian Mensah and Malachi Toney powered that win, while North Carolina hopes to deliver a major ACC upset in front of its home crowd.

Miami brings an explosive, efficient passing attack and a 7–0 start. The 4–3 Tar Heels have shown they can win close conference games, including road victories at Pittsburgh and Duke, but they need steadier offensive possessions against the Hurricanes.

things.title: Containing Miami's aerial attack
things.body: Mensah threw four touchdowns without a pick against Pitt, three to Toney. North Carolina must communicate against motion, contest throws at the catch point and force Miami to earn points in longer drives.

things.title: Can UNC keep the ball?
things.body: Billy Edwards Jr. and the Tar Heels need sustained first downs, fewer stalled drives and reliable field position. Giving Miami short fields or repeated quick possessions magnifies the mismatch.

things.title: Third-down protection
things.body: North Carolina has to protect Edwards well enough to hit Jordan Shipp and tight end Jelani Thurman on intermediate routes. Miami can play aggressively if UNC falls into predictable long-yardage downs.

paths_to_win.body: Keep Mensah upright, make Toney a consistent target and spread the ball around when Carolina shades coverage. Miami can create separation by turning early possessions into touchdowns and preventing extended UNC drives.

Play disciplined defense against explosive passes, finish tackles immediately and control the clock with Edwards and the rushing rotation. A turnover advantage and strong red-zone execution would keep the upset possible into the fourth.

players.name: Darian Mensah
players.body: The efficient Hurricanes passer has 22 touchdown passes and only one interception through seven games.

players.name: Malachi Toney
players.body: The record-setting receiver enters after 16 catches, 194 yards and three touchdowns against Pitt.

players.name: Mark Fletcher Jr.
players.body: Miami's physical running option helps punish defenses that overplay its passing threats.

players.name: Billy Edwards Jr.
players.body: His quick decisions and ball security will be essential against Miami's pressure.

players.name: Jordan Shipp
players.body: North Carolina's leading receiver offers a route-running answer when defenses crowd the line.

players.name: Benjamin Hall
players.body: The Tar Heels' leading rusher must help establish manageable third downs.

unit_edges.title: Miami passing game vs Carolina secondary
unit_edges.body: Miami's passing efficiency and Toney's recent production give the Hurricanes an advantage downfield. UNC's coverage has to prevent repeated explosive gains and limit yards after the catch.

unit_edges.title: UNC offense vs Miami defense
unit_edges.body: North Carolina has moved the ball in stretches but faces a sharper test of protection and situational execution. Miami can control the game by pressing Edwards and shutting down early-down rushing lanes.
